newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premium rises further on Tokyo stock tumble.
newsitem.headline: Japan premium rises further on Tokyo stock tumble.

text.p: The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks are charged when raising funds in the Euro interbank market -- rose on Friday due to the steep losses on the Tokyo stock market, money traders said.
Major Japanese city banks with comparatively good ratings paid a premium of 25 basis points (BPS) over the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.53125 percent.
This compared with a premium of 17 BPS a week ago.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares was down more than 450 points, or 2.26 percent, at 19,988 at 0500 GMT. Bank shares also extended their recent losses, traders said.
A senior bank trader said: "The premium has widened again due to the overall weakness in (Japanese) bank shares, which was even more accentuated by the Nikkei's dive today."
The premium resurfaced in late November after debt-laden Hanwa Bank Ltd was ordered to halt operations, traders said.
The premium for major Japanese city banks was close to zero before regulators stepped in because of the regional bank's debt problems, they said.
